answer: Each identity locks an 80-credit bond and tends one vine row paired with a mirror row under the same soil. An auditor harvests both rows and computes their yield delta; a delta above 12 percent, a missing mirror row, or a reused mirror row burns the bond. The vineyard fee rises: first row 26, kth row 26+8(k-1), 1000th 8018, so 1000 fake identities cost 4022000 plus 80000 at risk. New accounts start at the highest fee paid, so splitting cannot reset it. A rented-vine ring fails because its mirror row is paired, and the delta exposes reuse. An honest grower pays 26 once and recovers the bond.
